58401.etyen:
Internationalism; see English supernova. The complete term is attested in English astronomical writing by 1933. By surface analysis, super- (“exceptionally powerful”) + nova (“nova”).
The first element ultimately derives from Latin super- (“above, beyond”), from super, itself from Proto-Italic *super, from Proto-Indo-European *upér (“over, above”). The second derives from Latin nova, the feminine of novus (“new”), in stella nova (“new star”); novus continues Proto-Italic *nowos, from Proto-Indo-European *néwos (“new”).
Compare the corresponding international terms Norwegian Nynorsk supernova,

1005089.etyen:
The precise origin is uncertain. One possibility is borrowing from English Anny (“female given name”), with the spelling adapted in Norwegian to reflect the English pronunciation. English Anny is a dated form of Annie, originally a pet form of Ann. In this analysis, the name ultimately derives from Late Latin Anna (“female given name”), from Koine Greek Ἄννα (Ánna, “Anna”), from Biblical Hebrew חַנָּה (Ḥannāh, “Hannah; grace, favour”).
